teaser.en: A hooked-thorn scrambler whose small berries turn from red to purple-black, and birds strip them fast.

summary.en: *Chinyokola* is a spiny scrambling shrub with glossy leaves and small berries that ripen purple-black. The ripe fruit is edible.

about.en: *Scutia myrtina* is a spiny, often scrambling shrub up to about 6 m. Its spreading branches carry recurved thorns, usually in pairs, grey with shiny brown tips. The leaves are glossy mid-green, oval and up to 6 cm long. The small, creamy-green, bell-shaped flowers grow in clusters, and the berries, up to 1 cm across, turn from green to red and then purple-black when ripe.

where.en: It is widespread from Kenya to South Africa and Madagascar, and east to India and Vietnam. ICRAF notes that in the dry lowlands it is confined to riverine vegetation, places near pools and swamps, and the seashore, often on coral soils and termite mounds. At the coast it fruits from January to April.

uses.en: ICRAF records that the ripe fruit is eaten, and that the roots and leaves are used as medicine. The shrub also gives fodder and shade. Birds and squirrels eat the fruit so readily that seed is hard to collect. Pakia records no Digo use.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name *chinyokola* and lists it among the names that cannot be analysed. ICRAF gives the Giriama name *munyahi*. 'Cat-thorn' is a common English name for the species.

sources: Maundu, P. & Tengnäs, B. (eds) (2005) Useful Trees and Shrubs for Kenya, ICRAF — sheet Scutia myrtina: https://apps.worldagroforestry.org/usefultrees/pdflib/Scutia_myrtina_KEN.pdf
